chapter: Spokane and arrival in Los Angeles
title: First months in Los Angeles and first steady job
summary: He sat in at Hollywood and Watts clubs while living in a boarding house, then got his first steady trio job with a tenor and bass.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: So I went to Los Angeles. I didn't know anybody there. I had to do an awful lot of walking. And I started going up to Harlem, up to Watts, every night late... First I'd make all the clubs in Hollywood, and there was one or two or three that would let me sit in. Then I'd catch the last train, streetcar, out to Watts down by City College, and I'd go out and stay there all night. And when it was all over, I'd take the streetcar, come all the way back home, and go to bed. I was living in a boarding house, eight dollars a

week, board and room.
And every night I did the same thing, until finally a piano player... At one of the places they used to let me sit in, the piano player, for some reason, got something else and he quit. And I still had two weeks to go on my six months; they had a thing there that ....(?).... six months before you had take a steady job. And I had two weeks to go, and he got permission, and they hired me. And that was my first job in Los Angeles, steady job, with a bass, tenor saxophone and piano.

The guys were King Guyon(?) and a bass player named Bob Straw. And I don't know what happened to either one of them. I really don't. I know that Bob Straw married the waitress, and King Guyon(?) is supposed to have married some wealthy woman and moved back east here somewhere. I don't know. And I have never seen either one of them since.
Then this drummer started coming in, and he got me with bands he was playing with. He was playing with Mugsy Marcellino and Garwood Vann, and he got me in there -- and I started to play with those two bands.
